What does a DoS attack deny in the CIA triad?
column2: Availability (the "A") — by exhausting bandwidth, connection state, or application capacity.

#separator:: DoS vs DDoS — the defining difference?
column2: DoS = single source; DDoS = many distributed sources (a botnet), so you can't block one IP.

#separator:: What is DRDoS?
column2: Distributed Reflection DoS — attackers spoof the victim's IP and bounce traffic off reflectors, hiding the true origin.

#separator:: Botnet command chain — name the tiers.
column2: Bot herder → handlers (C2) → agents/zombies.

#separator:: The three DoS categories and what each exhausts?
column2: Volumetric (bandwidth/bps), Protocol-state (connection tables/pps), Application-layer L7 (CPU/RAM/threads/rps).

#separator:: Which category is a SYN flood?
column2: Protocol / state (L4) — it exhausts the TCP backlog with half-open connections.

#separator:: Which category is a UDP or ICMP flood?
column2: Volumetric — it saturates link bandwidth.

#separator:: Which category is Slowloris / HTTP flood?
column2: Application-layer (L7).

#separator:: SYN flood — mechanism?
column2: Send TCP SYNs and never complete the handshake; half-open connections pile up in SYN-RECV and exhaust the backlog.

#separator:: Countermeasure for a SYN flood (the mechanism)?
column2: SYN cookies — validate the handshake without allocating backlog until a valid ACK returns.

#separator:: UDP flood — what happens on the target?
column2: UDP blasted to random ports; host replies ICMP port-unreachable, burning bandwidth both directions.

#separator:: Smurf attack — protocol and method?
column2: Spoofed ICMP echo to a broadcast address; every host replies to the victim (reflection). Now dead.

#separator:: Fraggle attack — how does it differ from Smurf?
column2: Same idea but UDP (echo/chargen) to a broadcast address instead of ICMP.

#separator:: Ping of Death — mechanism?
column2: Oversized/fragmented ICMP exceeding 65,535 bytes crashes the IP stack. Patched.

#separator:: Teardrop — mechanism?
column2: Overlapping IP fragment offsets crash reassembly. Patched.

#separator:: Slowloris — how does it work and why is it dangerous?
column2: Opens many connections and sends partial HTTP headers slowly, holding sockets open; wins with almost no bandwidth.

#separator:: HTTP flood — why hard to filter?
column2: It's a flood of valid GET/POST requests, hard to distinguish from real users; needs WAF/rate-limit/CAPTCHA.

#separator:: Reflection — definition?
column2: Spoof the victim's IP as source, send small queries to open servers so the replies land on the victim.

#separator:: Amplification — definition?
column2: Choose a protocol whose reply is much larger than the request, multiplying the attacker's traffic.

#separator:: Amplification factor — formula?
column2: Response size ÷ request size.

#separator:: Why must amplification use UDP + spoofing?
column2: UDP is connectionless (no handshake), so the source IP can be forged; TCP's handshake would defeat spoofing.

#separator:: Amplification ranking (highest first)?
column2: memcached ≫ NTP ≫ CLDAP/DNS ≫ SSDP.

#separator:: NTP amplification trigger command?
column2: monlist (returns a long list of recent clients).

#separator:: memcached amplification — which UDP port?
column2: UDP 11211 (record-setting ~10,000–51,000× factor).

#separator:: hping3 — what is it used for here?
column2: Crafted TCP/UDP/ICMP packet generation — SYN floods with -S --flood --rand-source (lab only).

#separator:: LOIC / HOIC — what to know for the exam?
column2: Historic volumetric stress "cannons" — name-recognition only; do not deploy.

#separator:: Anti-spoofing countermeasure for reflection (name it)?
column2: BCP38 / uRPF ingress filtering at the network edge drops spoofed source addresses.

#separator:: Why can't a volumetric DDoS be absorbed at the host?
column2: The upstream link saturates before packets reach host defenses; push mitigation to CDN/anycast/cloud scrubbing.

#separator:: PDoS / phlashing — what is it?
column2: Permanent DoS: corrupts firmware/hardware to brick the device (e.g. BrickerBot), not a temporary outage.

#separator:: PAM: why keep the admin plane out-of-band?
column2: So a flooded data-plane doesn't starve SSH/RDP/console — you keep access to administer and recover.

#separator:: PAM: how is the Vault protected against a control-plane DoS?
column2: High availability + disaster recovery + distributed (satellite) vaults, plus a load-balanced PSM farm.

#separator:: PAM: what is break-glass access for during a DoS?
column2: A sealed, dual-control, monitored emergency path that works when normal auth is degraded; alert on any retrieval.
